items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: But I guess then he went back to Kansas City, and lo and behold the next time he showed up with Count Basie and that was it.

ctx.x: Jo Jones told me that, and one night

at Jim and Andy's, he was a little high and he was talking on about that. And a few months later I was doing some research and I came across an old DownBeat from the '30s, and sure enough there was the whole story. She wanted to do, "I Can't Get Started," and he wanted her to do the blues, and she said, "I'm not a blues singer," and he said, "You're not Basie's singer either," and fired her.

Well, I suppose in that case, you see, and again this brings up the subject of, well, now, how can I put it? It brings up the subject of doing what you're told to do. Now, like I say, Fletcher Henderson's band were independent and outspoken, and Billie Holiday was independent and outspoken. Now, John Hammond, he thought that because she was a black singer she had to sing the blues. He wasn't ready to accept her as a singer. He thought Billie Holiday, the blues, that's it.
